chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:
Trimming the nails and taking from the mustache from Friday to Friday is a protection from leprosy.

key_terms.أَخْذُ الشَّارِبِ: Akhdh al-Sharib - Taking from the mustache: shortening the mustache, considered part of the natural disposition (fitra) in Islamic hygiene
key_terms.أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْجُذَامِ: Aman min al-Judham - Protection from leprosy: indicates the prophetic tradition connecting regular hygiene with disease prevention
key_terms.تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظَافِرِ: Taqlim al-Azafir - Trimming the nails: part of the Islamic practice of personal grooming (fitra) recommended on Fridays

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about trimming nails and mustache on Friday as protection from leprosy?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that maintaining a weekly routine of trimming the nails and mustache from one Friday to the next serves as a protection against leprosy. This teaching, transmitted through a reliable chain of narrators, reflects the Islamic emphasis on regular personal hygiene as both a spiritual practice tied to the sanctity of Friday and a practical measure for disease prevention. In the context of early Islamic society, such prophetic traditions provided health guidance rooted in religious observance.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
